# Data

**Source:** synthetic, generated by `src/generate_data.py` (seed 42, reproducible). The brief allows "synthetic company ledgers"; the loan tape follows Lending Club columns.

| File | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `data/loans.csv` | 24,447 | Loans issued Jan 2024 - Oct 2026: amount, term, grade, rate, FICO, DTI, income, purpose, default flag |
| `data/gl_monthly.csv` | 220 | 10 accounts x 22 months (Jan 2025 - Oct 2026): actual and budget |
| `data/balance_sheet.csv` | 198 | 9 lines x 22 months |
| `data/portfolio_monthly.csv` | 22 | Originations, receivable, interest income, charge-offs |
| `data/loans_scored.csv` | 24,447 | Loans + score, risk band, model PD, train/test flag |

**How the ledger ties to the loans:** interest income = sum of balance x rate / 12 over live loans; charge-offs and the provision come from loans that default; the budget uses a planned balance and a planned 14.05% yield, so variances have real drivers.

**Using real data (Lending Club, Kaggle):** map columns to `loans.csv` names (`loan_amnt, term, int_rate, grade, annual_inc, dti, fico_range_low -> fico, revol_util, delinq_2yrs, inq_last_6mths -> inq_last_6m, emp_length, home_ownership, purpose, loan_status -> default_flag`, `issue_d -> issue_month` as YYYY-MM), keep the same file name, and rerun from `src/build_db.py` (skip `generate_data.py`). The ledger would then need real finance data or the same derivation.
